{"concepts_used":["GC-0072","GC-0115","GC-0131"],"decline_reason":"","declined":false,"citations":[{"ref":"TMA1995/s217A","quote":"(1) The Registrar must make available for public inspection prescribed documents that relate to a trade mark while they are held in the Trade Marks Office at or after the time particulars of the application for registration of the trade mark are published under section 30."},{"ref":"TMA1995/s217A","quote":"(2) A document may be prescribed for the purposes of subsection (1) wholly or partly by reference to the fact that it does not contain information covered by a requirement under section 226A. This does not limit the ways in which documents may be prescribed for those purposes."},{"ref":"TMM/Part61/1/1/1","quote":"1.1.1 Most documents in relation to a trade mark application will be made available for public access. This means that interested parties can obtain copies of trade mark documents provided that they pay a fee and that the documents are considered prescribed for the purposes of section 217A of the Trade Mark Act"},{"ref":"TMM/Part61/1/1/1","quote":"1.1.2 Anyone can request all or specific documents that are on file. This might be because they are considering whether to oppose a trade mark or they are interested in information that will assist in the registration of their own trade mark. Under section 217A, no reason is required to be provided."},{"ref":"TMM/Part61/5/5/1","quote":"Correspondence generated by IP Australia will generally become available for public inspection if it does not contain material identified at part 3.1."},{"ref":"TMM/Part61/6/6/1","quote":"As a TM Headstart is not a trade mark application and is not published under section 30 until the Part 2 fee has been paid any documents that are not part of the published application will not be made available for public inspection."},{"ref":"TMM/Part61/1/1/2","quote":"1.2.1 Trade mark applications filed before 27 March 2007 can be requested under the Freedom of Information (FOI) Act. 1.2.2 For trade marks filed after 27 March 2007, any document that is not considered Available for Public Inspection (API) can be applied for under the FOI Act."}],"answer":"**Which documents become public?**

- **Act:** Section 217A requires public inspection of **prescribed documents** relating to a trade mark, while held in the Trade Marks Office at or after publication of the application particulars under section 30. It does not require every document to be public. Documents may be prescribed by reference to their not containing information covered by a section 226A requirement. [TMA1995/s217A]
- **Manual practice:** Most application documents are available for public access. Anyone may request all or specific documents on file without giving a reason; obtaining copies requires a fee and the documents must be prescribed for section 217A purposes. [TMM/Part61/1/1/1]
- **Manual practice:** IP Australia correspondence generally becomes available for inspection unless it contains material identified in Manual part 3.1. That part and the prescribing Regulations are not supplied, so these passages do not establish the complete list of accessible documents or exclusions. [TMM/Part61/5/5/1; TMA1995/s217A]

**Does this include TM Headstart before the Part 2 fee is paid?**

**No, under the stated Manual practice.** The Manual says TM Headstart is not a trade mark application and is not published under section 30 until the Part 2 fee has been paid. Documents that are not part of the published application are not made available for public inspection. Payment should therefore not be treated as making every Headstart document public. [TMM/Part61/6/6/1]

**Separate access route — Manual practice:** Applications filed before 27 March 2007 may be requested under FOI; for trade marks filed after that date, documents not available for public inspection may be applied for under FOI. This describes a request route, not guaranteed disclosure. [TMM/Part61/1/1/2]"}
